extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and news editors/broadcasters
extracted.subtask_description: A daily/newspaper article reporting wartime events (Allied/German operations, capitulations, movements) with dateline, byline, and editorial sidelines such as pronunciation of place names. Typical audience is the general public and news professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names in the news — pronunciation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: NAMES IN THE NEWS AND TO PRONOUNCE THEM: (followed by a list of place names with phonetic/pronunciation hints such as 'YPRES ~-EE "PR CIN', 'PERONNE --PAY (LONG,', 'ARRAS--A'RAS (FIRST A AS IN ARM)', 'LILLE==LEEL', 'CALAIS=-KAL' A (FIRST A AS IN ACCEPT, LAST AS IN ACE')')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sidebar pronunciation guide for French and Belgian place names intended to help readers, announcers and reporters pronounce wartime place-names correctly. Contains phonetic respellings and parenthetical notes (e.g., which vowel sound to use). Presented under an Associated Press byline; used as an editorial aid rather than analytical content.
